## Checks

Each of these asks the same kind of question: **is Claudinite working in this repo** — declared,
converged, gated, scheduled. A repo can fail any of them silently, which is why they are checks and
not prose: the session that has lost its rules is the session least able to notice.

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claudinite-lifecycle-declared` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `rules-index-current` | critical | correctness | check: blocking |
| `claudinite-isolation` | high | complexity | check: blocking |
| `conformance-workflow` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `conformance-work-scope` | high | correctness | check: advisory |
| `scheduler-workflow-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `legacy-shape-in-use` | medium | complexity | check: advisory |
| `skill-loaded-before-editing` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `skills-index-current` | medium | correctness | check: blocking |

What goes wrong when one fires:

- `claudinite-lifecycle-declared` — this pack's entry is gone from `.claudinite-settings.json`, so none of the rules above run and the session cannot tell.
- `rules-index-current` — the generated index is missing, stale or unimported: the repo's packs contribute no prose to any session.
- `claudinite-isolation` — the repo's own code reaches into `.claudinite/`, so the next canon refactor is a breaking migration for code the canon does not own (a declared `forbidReferences` barrier edge).
- `conformance-workflow` — nothing in CI runs the world sweep unfiltered on a pull request, so conformance is ungated and the maintenance PR never lands.
- `conformance-work-scope` — CI gates the tree but not the change, so every commit-scoped rule is enforced only where a session's Stop hook happens to run.
- `scheduler-workflow-shape` — the vendored scheduler's cron, concurrency or dispatch guard has drifted: staggering, double-run safety or manual runs break.

The **task contract** and its checks are deliberately NOT here. Those ask whether a task is
*written* correctly, which is authoring; every check above asks whether Claudinite is *working* in
this repo. They live with the rest of the authoring surface.

The scope cuts the other way too: a rule about how the **canon's own** content is maintained is not
this pack's, however much it looks like one. `catalog-completeness` — `packs/README.md` lists every
`packs/<name>/` — reads as Claudinite machinery and is not: it can only fire in the corpus repo, and
what it guards is a hand-maintained index, not a member's status. It stays with the other
doc-integrity rules.

`skill-loaded-before-editing` is the Stop-time half of **path-scoped skills**: a skill names
the files it must be loaded for under `force-load-on-file-edits-paths` in its SKILL.md frontmatter
`metadata` (the harness's own `paths` is a limiter on when it offers a skill, so it cannot carry
this), the engine's PreToolUse guard holds a file tool aimed there until the session has
loaded that skill, and this rule catches the edits the guard never saw (a `sed`, a heredoc) by
asking the diff the same question. Both read one resolver,
`engine/pack_loader/path-scoped-skills.mjs`. A load is a `Skill` tool call or a `Read` of the
skill's own SKILL.md. `skills-index-current` keeps the generated
`.claudinite/claudinite-skills.GENERATED.md` — every mounted skill with what loads it, the
scoped ones first — naming what the declared packs actually bundle.

## Skills

| Skill | For |
|---|---|
| [`adopt-claudinite`](skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md) | setting a project up on Claudinite for the first time — mount, hooks, checks, skills — and re-baselining one to pick up updates |
| [`adopt-pack`](skills/adopt-pack/SKILL.md) | adding a pack to a repo that already runs Claudinite: declare, interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land |

The adoption skills bundle two more checks of the same kind, over the answers a member stores
against each declared pack's questions:

| Check | Severity | Reason | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adoption-answers-pending` | medium | complexity | check: blocking |
| `interview-answer-stale` | low | complexity | check: advisory |

## Tasks

| Task | frequency | Runs when |
|---|---|---|
| `update` | daily (02:00 anchor) | the mount is behind the canon, or a declared pack moved |
| `adopt-requested-packs` | daily | the repo carries an open pack-adoption request |

`update` is the per-repo self-refresh — the task that converges a member's mount and stamps it. It
is why `claudinite-lifecycle-declared` is blocking: a member runs `update` from its **vendored** copy, and
`discoverTasks` finds only a literally-declared pack's tasks, so a repo that loses this pack's entry
loses its self-refresh, and nothing is left that could deliver it one. That is also why the task
arrived here a change later than the rest of the pack — it moved only once every non-dormant member's
declaration had been read back and confirmed to carry `core`.

Records for `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/pack.mjs`'s `version` field, one row per bump. The
rows below are version-numbered comments that used to sit beside `version:` in the manifest,
moved here verbatim; nothing earlier than the first of them was backfilled, and a bump with no
comment (like 60821.2) was never recorded to begin with. Every bump from here forward adds its
own row.

| 60903.8 | 2026-09-03 | `promote-to-canon` adds a rule: finding which check enforces a given rule reads that pack's own `declared-checks.json` directly rather than grepping the engine's check-runner source (#1372). |
| 60903.7 | 2026-09-03 | `promote-to-canon` adds three prose rules: a file a vendored module references but that's absent from the mount is evidence about the vendor set, not the canon; diagnose a stuck `[claudinite-task]` `needs-human` issue by what actually landed rather than by comment volume; grep the engine for a live naming convention before inventing a fleet-wide secret/endpoint/routine id; and run `check_the_world.mjs` locally before pushing (#1204). |
| 60903.6 | 2026-09-03 | `promote-to-canon` adds a Shepherd rule: re-run `converge-wiring.mjs --badges` on a pack rename or removal, not just on adoption via `adopt-pack` — otherwise the README's packs badge row goes silently stale (#1157). |
| 60903.4 | 2026-09-03 | `legacy-shape-in-use` states the window a repo has to act on its own finding rather than claiming the removal waits on nobody carrying the shape (#1652). |
| 60903.3 | 2026-09-03 | `legacy-shape-in-use` — an advisory over this repo's own declaration and stamp for every shape the engine merely tolerates: the retired settings-file name, the `claudinite`/`maintenance` blocks, top-level `packConfig`, `taskScheduler.endpoints`, the `local_packs/` declaration prefix, a renamed or absorbed pack id, an integer version and the `updates` mechanism alias. Each finding names the edit that moves the repo forward; each tolerance is scheduled for removal on no member still carrying it (#1637). |

---
name: git-github-advanced
description: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
---

# Portable git & GitHub procedures

A GitHub procedure the consuming repo's own docs set — its merge command, when it opens a PR, its generated-file merge rules — wins over anything below.

## Updating an issue's status: comment, don't overwrite

To post a **status update** on an issue (the lifecycle's "update the issue's status" step), use `add_issue_comment`. **Don't** reach for `issue_write` with `method: update` — that edits the issue itself and **replaces the whole body**, silently wiping the original description. Reserve `issue_write`/`update` for genuinely editing the issue (retitling, rewriting the body on purpose).

The same tool's `labels` field carries the same trap for a different part of the issue: it **replaces the whole label set**, not just the ones you name. Adding or removing one label without also reading and re-sending every label already on the issue silently drops the rest — read the issue's current labels first, compute the full set with your one change applied, and write that back whole.

## An auto-merge refusal is not a verdict — read the PR's state, then act

`enable_pr_auto_merge` only accepts a PR whose required checks are still **pending**, so its refusals answer *timing and configuration*, never the change. Take each at face value and stop:

- *"already in clean status (all checks passed)"* — the checks finished before you got there. That's the green light: `merge_pull_request` directly.

1	# Working discipline
2	
3	- **Starting any requested change** — begin from the *problem*, not the solution, in any
4	  repository and not just this one. Reach an explicit shared understanding with the owner of the
5	  problem the change is meant to solve **and** agreement that the requested change is the best way
6	  to solve it; a different fix, or none, may serve better.
7	
8	- **Replying to an owner comment** — open with an explicit classification line,
9	  `Comment class: correction | feature | process-change | other`, where `other` covers questions,
10	  approvals and command phrases and a mixed comment names each part. An automation dispatch prompt
11	  is a comment too: class `other`, in your *first* substantive reply rather than at the end of the
12	  run. Put the class **alone on the line** and any explanation on the next one: the line is scanned
13	  for *every* class token on it, so restating the menu declares all of them. A class cannot be taken
14	  back, and a clean re-declaration further down does not override the first.
15	
16	- **Acting on a correction** — you misunderstood something. Repair the shared understanding, then
17	  rework what the misread already touched; the artifact changes as much as the correction demands,
18	  but a correction never adds a new requirement or rule.
19	
20	- **Acting on a feature** — agree on the requirement, record it in the project's requirements
21	  document (its executable spec, where it keeps one), write the test that proves it and watch it
22	  fail, then implement until it passes.
23	
24	- **Acting on a process change** — the owner is changing *how* work is done. Land it as durable
25	  rules in the project's local scope, its own local packs (in Claudinite itself, its packs), routed
26	  through the mechanism promotion ladder (platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose).
27	  Promoting a rule into the shared canon is the growth lifecycle's separate call, not the
28	  interactive session's.
29	
30	- **Choosing what goes on that ladder** — only a rule that constrains *how work is done* and
31	  outlives any one feature; a checkable signature doesn't earn a rule its place. Reject two shapes
32	  outright: a check that asserts particular code exists or still reads a particular way (it pins a
33	  point in time), and a rule derivable from the product's requirements (that is a requirement —
34	  take it to the feature path, the requirements document and the test that proves it).
35	
36	- **Landing a rule anywhere on the ladder** — author the assurance first, the check the future
37	  world must satisfy, execute it and watch it fail, and only then make the fixes that turn it green.
38	  At the prose rung, where no check can carry an in-flight judgment rule, the equivalent step is
39	  showing the corpus doesn't already cover the rule before writing it.
40	
41	- **Building a mechanism for a behavior** — verify against a real run that it isn't already
42	  provided.
43	
44	- **Building release, deploy, versioning or CI plumbing** — look for the shared pack that owns it
45	  first; copying a mechanic from a sibling repo is the tell that it belongs centrally. If no pack
46	  owns it, report the gap rather than author a third copy.
47	
48	- **Finishing a change** — watch it work **now**; never park it on "check tomorrow". What a task
49	  costs is its shelf-life, the time from starting it until everyone can forget about it.
50	
51	- **Changing scheduled or unattended machinery** — force a run now (the scheduler's wake lever, a
52	  `workflow_dispatch`, the fleet-wide force sweep) and watch it to a terminal state rather than wait
53	  for its next natural run.
54	
55	- **Planning a migration** — prefer the design that converges in one forced pass to the one that
56	  trickles across nightly cycles, accept legacy input at the door so nothing has to wait for
57	  stragglers, and drive the stragglers with a standing mechanism rather than a phase someone must
58	  remember to close. Write every phase's code — the cleanup, the destructive tail and every
59	  legacy tolerance's removal included — before asking for approval, and chain each execution step
60	  to the verification of the one before it rather than to anyone's memory;
61	  [writing-migration-plans](skills/writing-migration-plans/SKILL.md) owns that ordering and the
62	  chain's mechanics.
63	
64	- **Adding a legacy tolerance** (a dual read, an accepted old spelling, a shim) — it is
65	  scaffolding, not a feature: ship it with an advisory that fires where the old shape is still in
66	  use, and with its removal already a link in the migration's chain, due one stated convergence
67	  window after that advisory reaches the holders. (2)
68	
69	- **Choosing an automerge policy for a PR or a chain link** — write it as a prediction of the
70	  change's shape, the folders and kinds you expect the diff to touch, and never widen it to fit the
71	  diff that arrived: a policy that fails is the speed bump that puts a person back on the trail,
72	  not an error to route around. (1)
73	
74	- **Predicting a change that could delete production data or degrade the experience past what a
75	  later PR undoes** — its policy is `nothing`, whatever its diff class; irreversibility is the
76	  first of the two things review here exists to catch. (1)
77	
78	- **Handing over a change whose diff reached more folders or files than its request implied** —
79	  say so, and name the abstraction that would have kept it in one place: the reviewer reads which
80	  folders moved to judge whether the change made sense, and a wide diff for a small ask is the
81	  growth lesson review is for, not a defect. (1)
82	
83	- **Retiring a system by folding its function into another** — verify the *machinery* came over,
84	  not just its historical output: a copied directory of the old system's artifacts visually
85	  launders the absence of the live generator that produced them, so audit for the generator
86	  explicitly, in the same pass, rather than inferring it from the presence of past output. And
87	  before dropping a carried-over aggregate on the assumption "the next run recomputes it," check
88	  whether the new generator's own inputs retain the same history the aggregate already holds — a
89	  stateless recompute over inputs the new system keeps only for a bounded window starts the series
90	  shorter than a file carried over from elsewhere already carries.
91	
92	- **When verifying now is genuinely impossible** (an external release window, an upstream fix in
93	  flight, an effect that only appears once the change is deployed, converged or loaded by a later
94	  session) — the follow-up is a mechanism that comes to you, never a human's memory and never an
95	  offer to the owner to go and check later. File it with
96	  [verify-in-production](skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md), unasked, **once the PR has
97	  merged** and never before — a PR can be rejected, and a still-open branch can be rewritten
98	  under you, either of which strands a verification whose premise never reached `main`. The
99	  skill owns both halves — whether this change needs one at all (most don't; a test that ran is
100	  already the mechanism), and the issue that states what puts the change in production and what
101	  proves it works there.
102	
103	- **Finishing a larger element** — one that earned a design doc or a phased tracking issue — a
104	  point verification is not enough: schedule the review that comes back once the element has
105	  lived in production about a week, asking whether it is working, misused, overused or underused
106	  against its real record — with the brief written at design time, expected amounts, signals and
107	  the metrics that measure them included, never improvised when the review runs.
108	  [production-retrospective](skills/production-retrospective/SKILL.md) owns the trigger, the
109	  brief, and the lane's other classes — canon, local-pack and fleet alike.
110	
111	- **Receiving feedback that flags a misunderstanding** — check whether the artifact is already
112	  correct before expanding it; if it is, say so and push back rather than edit.
113

22	- **A change-gated routine must exclude its *own* writes from its triggers, or it feeds itself.** A routine that commits to, files issues in, or emits artifacts into the same repos it monitors will re-fire on its own output unless every trigger filters it out: its own maintenance commits must not count as "the project changed" (match them by bot-author / `[skip ci]` / a subject convention and exclude — and keep that matcher current with the wording the routine actually writes, or a near-miss silently reads as real work); its own standing-tracker/issue updates must not count as activity (a tracker rewritten every run always sits inside a fixed lookback window, so it re-triggers forever); its own generated plan/report artifact must not count as a repo change. The tell is a routine that fires every cycle on a fleet that is actually quiet. Treat "the routine's inputs never include the routine's outputs" as an invariant when wiring any change-detection signal.
23	- When an unattended routine takes an **irreversible or outward-facing action** (closing an issue, deleting a branch, sending a message), the spec must **define the trigger condition concretely and default to the safe path** — not just name the action. A bare "close if done" invites a wrong close on a superficial match; "close *only* when the ask is verifiably true of the target's current state — else comment" cannot. State what counts as the condition and where to verify it, and make the reversible option (leave it, comment, escalate) the default whenever the check is inconclusive.
24	- A `[Merge Without Review]` security warning on a task's own unattended merge is expected, not a finding to escalate — adjudicate it in one step. When a task's declared delivery policy is auto-merge and its target's checks require no human approval (or the arm is rejected `clean status` and a direct merge is the sanctioned path), the harness still flags the completion with a security warning because no human approval appears in the transcript — that is the harness reporting the *shape* of the action, not evaluating whether it was licensed. Confirm the task's declared delivery policy and its outcome ceiling permit the merge, then converge normally; escalating every occurrence to human review would wedge a routine that is designed to merge unattended.

+- **Before concluding a subagent whose handle went unreachable left no progress, check every place its output could have landed — not just git state and the dispatch's own PR comments.** A subagent that hits something worth escalating may record that as a filed tracker issue rather than a commit; a recovery check that reads only local git log and the dispatch PR's comments can miss it entirely, read "nothing survived," and relaunch a duplicate investigation that reproduces — and re-files — the same finding.
+- **A lost subagent's handle going unreachable is not evidence it made no progress — check every channel it could have written to, not just git.** A subagent whose process is interrupted or restarted mid-task can have already produced real output through a side channel (filing a tracking issue, say) moments before going silent. A recovery check that reads only git log/status and a dispatch PR's own comments will read that as "nothing survived" and relaunch a fresh subagent from a from-scratch briefing — which re-investigates the same ground and produces a duplicate. Before asserting "no progress" in a relaunch briefing, also search for anything the lost subagent may have filed (issues, comments), not just commits.
+- **Don't perform a dispatched subagent's work yourself before its result is actually in hand.** Backgrounding a subagent to do X and then, before its completion notification (or your own scheduled wakeup) arrives, independently doing X yourself makes the subagent's run entirely redundant the moment it does report back. Once you've stated a wait-for-subagent plan, actually wait — check what its notification says before taking the action it was dispatched to take.
+- Never act *on* the shared checkout while a background agent is live in it, either: don't amend a commit the subagent already pushed, and don't relay a "fix" instruction built from a misread of its in-flight state. If the checkout-back or the corrective action is itself refused by the session's own permission classifier, that refusal is the tell — a live subagent is using the checkout — so don't retry or force it; leave the branch alone and wait for the subagent to finish.
+- Once a source is delegated to a background subagent, reading or re-analyzing it yourself while the dispatch is running is wasted work, not a safety net. A subagent dispatched to mine one file, log, or page fully owns it, and the orchestrator's own parallel read of the same source computes nothing the subagent doesn't already report — it only burns tool calls and wall-clock alongside a dispatch that will hand back the same findings anyway. Wait on the dispatch with no tool call, or spend the interim on genuinely different work; read the subagent's report when it lands rather than re-deriving it in parallel.
+- Before concluding a lost background subagent "made no progress" — its handle went unreachable after a genuine worker restart, and you need to decide whether to relaunch — check every channel it could have written to, not only git state and the dispatch thread's own comments. A subagent can produce real output through a channel a narrow recovery check doesn't think to look at (filing its own tracking issue, for one, moments before it went down), and checking only git log/status plus the parent conversation's comments reads as "nothing survived" when something did. Relaunching a fresh subagent from scratch on that false premise duplicates the lost one's work. Search broadly — issues, PRs, comments — across the write surface a subagent could have used before declaring nothing landed.
+- Catching a flawed prompt or input right after dispatching a background subagent — send a follow-up message to *that same* agent to resume it, never a fresh redispatch over the identical source. A redispatch runs a full second pass in parallel with the first, at full cost, even when the original would have handled the flaw fine on its own or needs only a small correction. Prefer pointing a subagent at a reference file's *path* to read for itself over pasting its content inline in the prompt, too — cheaper, and immune to the class of bug where the pasted content is left as an unfilled placeholder.
 - **Parallel background agents that each dump external content to disk need a collision-proof filename, not a shared generic one.** Subagents dispatched from one session share its scratchpad directory, so a fleet of them each told (or defaulting) to write the same generic path — a bare `log.jsonl`, `out.txt` — race on it: one agent's write can land mid-read by another, producing a truncated or mixed-content file with no error from either side. Give each agent's output a name that can't collide with its siblings' — the source item's own filename, or the agent's own session id — never a shared default.
+- **Once a source is delegated to a background subagent, don't also mine or duplicate-analyze it yourself while waiting.** Racing ahead with your own read of the same file the subagent owns wastes its entire run when it comes back with the same answer, and produces nothing when it doesn't; either wait with no tool call, or spend the interim on work no subagent already owns. And if you catch a flawed prompt moments after dispatching — a wrong path, an unfilled placeholder — send a **follow-up message to resume that same agent**, never a brand-new dispatch over the identical source: a redispatch runs a full second pass in parallel with the first, at full cost, even when the original would have handled it fine on its own.
+- **While a background subagent is dispatched to analyze or mine a file, don't also read that same file yourself.** Its own output will land on the same conclusions you'd reach re-reading it, so a parent that races ahead in parallel spends real tool calls computing what the subagent is already computing. Wait on the dispatched result (idle, or genuinely independent work) rather than shadowing its read.
+- **After a dispatched subagent's handle becomes unreachable (a lost session, a worker restart), checking only git state and the dispatching PR's own comments is not enough to tell whether it made progress.** Its real output may be a filed GitHub issue rather than a commit — both clean git and PR-comment state is exactly what a subagent whose only artifact was an issue leaves behind. Before asserting "no progress survived" and relaunching a fresh subagent from scratch, also search issues for anything the lost one may have filed; skipping that step is how a relaunch re-investigates the same finding and files a duplicate.
 
 ## Structuring a routine as prose + scripts

 - **When driving a CI-gated merge via API/MCP poll rather than the shell, merge on an already-green required check — don't trigger or wait for a duplicate run.** A push already ran CI on the head commit; opening a PR on the same commit fires an identical second run that adds no signal. If the check isn't yet green, poll on a rolling backoff (e.g. 5 s → 10 s → 15 s → 30 s) until it settles; never tight-poll; and don't subscribe for green — CI success transitions are frequently not delivered as webhook events, so the green signal never arrives.
 - **When an action you take kicks off an async downstream process whose output matters to what happens next (a merge triggering a build/publish/deploy), don't report the task done until that process completes and its output exists — poll for it.** Reporting at the trigger point races the async process: a follow-up action taken right after (e.g. "now ship this") would then operate on the stale prior output instead of the one just triggered.
 - **In a multi-stage agent pipeline, every failure exit must converge to the same human-triage state.** A setup-phase failure (page download, authentication, scaffolding) that posts a comment but leaves the original trigger label in place makes the item look unprocessed rather than blocked, defeating the escalation mechanism. Treat every failure mode — pre-agent setup, agent bail, post-agent quality check — as equivalent from the triage perspective: all must resolve to the same visible state (e.g. a comment naming what failed, plus the trigger label removed).
+- **Once a piece of work is fully delegated to a background subagent, don't also do it yourself while waiting.** Re-reading or re-analyzing the same source a dispatched subagent already owns wastes the delegation — either the parent's own pass duplicates what the subagent is about to report (redundant work for nothing), or it lands first and the subagent's later, possibly better-informed result is thrown away. ## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user's explicit request in this session: "Please create a new PR with all the changes from those 9 PRs [1021, 1157, 1204, 1345, 1372, 1409, 1451, 1524, 1661 in missingbulb/claudinite]. I'll review it once and decide what stays and what not. After moving all the changes - close the PRs above."
   
   This is a two-part task:
   (a) Consolidate all changes from the 9 already-rebased PRs into ONE new PR against main, and
   (b) After the new PR captures all changes, close the 9 original PRs.
   
   Critical interpretation I adopted: since the user will personally review and decide what stays, I must NOT deduplicate or editorially prune overlapping/near-duplicate content across the 9 source PRs — I keep everything from every PR, even when two PRs add near-identical bullets with different wording, and let the user's review sort it out.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Git cherry-pick as the consolidation mechanism (chosen over `git merge` to avoid merge commits that could trip the repo's own `squash-merge-history` check, and to keep history linear)
   - Claudinite pack versioning scheme: date-encoded version strings like '60903.5' = (year-2020)(MMDD).counter, with counter incrementing for same-day bumps; each pack's `pack.mjs` `version` field must match the top row of its `VERSIONS.md` table
   - `packs/<pack>/VERSIONS.md` — append-new-row-at-top convention, one row per version bump, format `| version | date | description (#PR-number) |`
   - `packs/<pack>/README.md` — contains a "Rules (`RULES.md`)" markdown table that must have one row per RULES.md bullet, in the same order, with exact word counts; verified via `node --test engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs`. Row labels must be under 8 words (a separate assertion in that test).

{"number":1157,"title":"Promote portable lessons from Shepherd and TLDR","body":"Refs #99. `canon-curation/growth-promote` run over the local packs of `missingbulb/Shepherd`, `missingbulb/TLDR` and `missingbulb/WIP` (this window's Context — the members whose local packs changed). WIP's local pack is still empty (`<!-- Nothing yet. -->`), so nothing to read there.

**Six prose additions** (`packs/basics/RULES.md`, `packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md`, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md`) — all judgment/runtime-behavior items with no reliable static signature a check could carry:

- **Shepherd** → `basics/RULES.md` (Harness-tool contracts) — check first whether an `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided (a loaded rule, a read away, the recommended option being the status quo), and batch every open decision into **one** question.
- **Shepherd** → `basics/RULES.md` (Working discipline) — retiring a system by folding its function into another: verify the *generator* moved, not just its historical output, and check whether the new generator's own inputs retain the same history a carried-over aggregate already holds before dropping it on the assumption "the next run recomputes it."
- **Shepherd** → `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — a session scoped to a **single** repo denies a cross-repo call outright, not merely filters; check the session's actual scope, and look for the answer in what you already have (an issue/PR body often already carries it), before spending a call rediscovering the denial. (Sharpens the existing "When access is scoped to an explicit repo list" section with the single-repo case.)
- **Shepherd** → `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — `search_code`'s index can lag and silently undercount when enumerating a population across many repos; cross-check against a direct enumeration before trusting it as complete (measured: 3 of 11 affected repos via search alone).
- **Shepherd** → `git-github-advanced/SKILL.md` — after a bulk/fleet-wide sweep, subscribe to **every** PR it leaves open, not a sample — the unsubscribed ones get no activity signal and fall back to real-cost re-polling.
- **Shepherd** → `claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md` — re-run `converge-wiring.mjs --badges` on a pack **rename or removal**, not just on adoption via the `adopt-pack` skill (which already covers the addition case) — otherwise the README's packs badge row goes silently stale and only resurfaces later as a blocking `reference-integrity` finding.

Versions bumped: `basics` 60821.1 → 60821.2, `git-github` 60820.2 → 60821.1, `claudinite-lifecycle` 60821.1 → 60821.2.

**Notable rejections (dedup verified against the current corpus and open PRs, not memory):**

- **TLDR's `comment-class-menu` check** (advisory, catches a `Comment class:` line that declares extra classes via a same-line explanation or a pasted menu) — not promoted. This exact lesson, generalized as `comment-classification-form`, is already proposed in the still-open PR #1021 (from a prior promote run over TLDR). More pointedly: #1114 (2026-08-20, one day before this run) is the owner's own deliberate, measured call to **remove** a check in this same area (`comment-classification.mjs`, 204 blocking firings / 21% of all blocking findings in 31 days) and keep only the prose. Re-adding a check here — even TLDR's narrower, advisory-severity one — reopens a question the owner just settled; it's #1021's (and the owner's) call, not this run's to re-litigate or duplicate.
- **TLDR's `release-root-version-align` check** — TLDR's own local delta over its vendored `chrome-extension-daily-release.yml` stub (a repo-root `package.json` alignment step, tied to specific commits/PR numbers). Not portable — stays local.
- **Shepherd's fleet-activity-filtering lesson** (filter the machine's own bookkeeping out of activity rankings, via `isDispatchTitle`) — grounded entirely in Shepherd's own fleet-enforcer role; there is exactly one fleet enforcer, so it isn't reusable by a future project.
- **Shepherd's PR-CI-polling lesson** (poll `get_check_runs`, don't call `enable_pr_auto_merge` before checks start) — already covered by `git-github-advanced`'s "An auto-merge refusal is not a verdict" and "To read a PR's CI result" sections.
- **Shepherd's `search_issues`-by-exact-title lesson** — already covered near-verbatim by `git-github-advanced`'s "Cap and qualify every list/search call" section ("When you already know the exact title, don't search at all — list and match it yourself").

Verified: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2406/2406 green (unshallowed the checkout first; one pre-existing failure from the shallow default clone cleared before any of this PR's changes were applied). `check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 68 advisory, none touching the files this PR changes.

Every candidate was generalized first, then judged against [item-routing.md](.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/item-routing.md)'s worthiness bar and deduped against the whole corpus (not just the file it would land in). A large fraction of what these five repos' local packs carried was already covered — several near-verbatim, confirming the canon was already built from these or sibling incidents (the search_issues/list_issues token-limit cluster, the Playwright/headless-browser sandbox traps, the sync-local-main-is-a-convenience rule, the shallow-clone merge-base trap, "a pack states how we work, never what the product does," and the extract-side "never capture a rule that teaches routing around a permission denial" guard). Those are left alone.

**What lands here:**

- **basics** — a doc-claims-falsified rule that generalizes beyond privacy/data claims; two harness-tool-contract entries (a `wait` split across two Bash calls is a no-op; verify a shell tool exists before building a poll loop's condition on it); a golden-image-flake reproduction rule in `writing-tests` (use the harness's own pixel comparator, not a byte/hash compare); a browser-DevTools-first rule in `bug-investigation` for live-data bug reports on apps with multiple caching layers; an anchored-JSON-edit rule in `repo-text-sweeps`.
- **git-github** (`git-github-advanced` skill) — the write-scope-boundary pattern (patch-on-issue when your push access doesn't reach the repo that owns the fix); prefer an amend over `filter-branch` when a finding's own fix is already an amend; a Monitor/curl false-positive reading an error body as "zero pending"; a CI-artifact-blocked-in-sandbox reproduction path (`get_job_logs` + a large tail, not the blob-storage link); the long-running-workflow-races-a-scheduled-writer recovery (re-derive, never merge, generated bytes).
- **claudinite-growth** (`unattended-agents` skill) — sharpens the existing shared-working-directory false-positive bullet (never amend a subagent's pushed commit, never relay a fabricated fix, don't force a denied checkout-back); a new bullet on a lost/restarted subagent's other output channels (it may have filed an issue before going silent); a new bullet on not racing your own dispatched subagent's work.
- **claudinite-lifecycle** — a vendoring-omission-vs-canon-gap rule; diagnosing a stuck `[claudinite-task]` `needs-human` issue by what actually landed rather than by comment volume; grepping the engine for a live naming convention before inventing a fleet-wide secret/endpoint/routine id; running `check_the_world.mjs` locally before pushing (it's CI-only, not run by the Stop hook).
- **ios** — fills the stub with its first two worked-example rules: the agent's own sandbox has no macOS/Swift toolchain (often network-blocked, not merely absent), and an Apple Developer Documentation page is JS-rendered — fetch its JSON mirror instead.

Every touched pack has its `version` bumped and a dated `VERSIONS.md` row. Write surface is `packs/` only. Full local suite (2520/2520) and `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` (0 blocking) both green after the edits, including after re-wrapping two files to clear a line-length advisory my own additions tripped.

Closes #1202

{"number":1345,"title":"Promote-to-canon: lessons from MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd, VascularColoring, WIP","body":"Refs #1308 — growth-promote run over target members MissingBulbWebsite, Shepherd, VascularColoring, WIP.

All items land as **prose** (no rung-3 check candidate was confidently authorable — every item is judgment/behavioral, or the pattern spans arbitrary scripts and project-specific paths).

| Pack | Origin | Landed rule |
|---|---|---|
| `basics` | Shepherd | Check whether an `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided before asking; batch several open decisions into one question. |
| `basics` | MissingBulbWebsite | Never publish a public claim about a real, named person from a secondary/data-broker source when the primary source is blocked — ask instead. |
| `git-github` (`git-github-advanced`) | MissingBulbWebsite | `codeload.github.com` can be blocked by a sandbox's egress proxy where ordinary `git clone` isn't — use `git clone --depth 1` instead of a tarball fetch. |
| `git-github` (`git-github-advanced`) | WIP | Resolve a wait on a GitHub Actions run/check through exactly one mechanism (the `Monitor` tool, or direct polling) — never a background sleep alongside a separate blocking poll. |
| `basics` (`writing-tests` skill) | WIP | Sharpened the existing see-it-fail restore guidance: restoring a **staged** destructive test mutation needs `git checkout HEAD -- <file>`, not a bare `git checkout -- <file>` (which restores from the index and leaves the staged mutation in place). |
| `basics` (`repo-text-sweeps` skill) | WIP | Patch a hand-maintained JSON config as anchored text, never a `json.load`/`json.dumps` round-trip (reorders keys, changes indent, re-escapes strings with nothing failing). |
| `claudinite-growth` (`unattended-agents` skill) | Shepherd + WIP | Don't duplicate work already delegated to a background subagent — wait for and read its output first. (Two of this run's four target repos independently reported this.) |
| `claudinite-growth` (`unattended-agents` skill) | Shepherd | Don't manufacture a no-op tool call while waiting on a background subagent with nothing to do — state the wait in plain text instead. |
| `claudinite-growth` (`extract-from-conversations` skill) | WIP | A captured `conversation-logs` JSONL line can be large enough to overflow a raw `Read`'s token cap even at a small offset/limit — check line lengths first. |
| `flutter` | WIP | Real file/image I/O inside `testWidgets` must run inside `tester.runAsync`, or the fake-async test zone never completes it and the case hangs. |

Ten distilled, portable lessons, generalized and deduped against the whole corpus, all landing as prose (none had a narrow-enough signature for a check on their own):

- **`packs/claudinite-tasks/RULES.md`** (new file) — a step that talks to GitHub's REST API directly (`converge-item.mjs`, `gh.mjs`, a hand-rolled CI-status poll) cannot run from an ordinary agent session; recognize the failure signature (`GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set`, then a 401 or proxied 403) on sight and never hand-replicate the transition via `issue_write`'s overwriting `labels` field. Corroborated independently in three of the four target members.
- **`git-github/skills/git-github-advanced`** — `list_pull_requests`'s `head` filter needs an `owner:` qualifier or it silently mismatches; Claude Code Web's PR-diff view can silently drop a root-level file addition (verify with `git ls-files`); wait on a GitHub Actions run/PR check through exactly one mechanism, never a background sleep alongside direct polling.
- **`basics/RULES.md`** — a `ToolSearch` miss against an MCP server whose roster is already fully named in the deferred-tools listing is the whole answer, don't reword and retry; a tall screenshot rejected after a width/byte downscale needs quartering by height, not halving (the delivery channel caps pixel height independently).
- **`basics/skills/writing-tests`** — sharpens the existing restore-after-mutation advice for the case where the mutation was staged before restoring (`git checkout HEAD -- <file>`, not the bare form, which restores from the index).
- **`claudinite-growth/skills/unattended-agents`** — a fan-out orchestrator must not duplicate work it already delegated to a background subagent, and resumes that same agent on a flawed just-dispatched prompt rather than redispatching a new one over the same source. Corroborated independently in two of the four members.
- **`node/RULES.md`** — a local pass proves nothing about a pinned CI Node version; the agent sandbox's Node can be newer than what CI actually pins.
- **`claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md`** — finding which check enforces a given rule reads that pack's own `declared-checks.json` directly rather than grepping engine source.

Every edited pack's `version` is bumped with a matching `VERSIONS.md` row; the rules index is regenerated for the new `claudinite-tasks/RULES.md` import. `check_the_world.mjs` and `check_the_work.mjs` both run clean (0 blocking).

Rejected/skipped this run (leaving them local for a future pass rather than promoting): a couple of narrower items (a specific external doc-site mirror workaround, a Flutter-specific cwd assumption) didn't clear the bar cleanly enough to promote today; several other candidates across the four members were already covered by existing canon prose and are left as-is in their local packs (dedup, not a gap).

Never arms auto-merge — for the owner to review.

## Promoted

- **`basics`** — new check `no-conflict-markers`: a leftover merge-conflict marker line in any scanned file. Lifted near-verbatim (ClaudiniteWebsite's own check was already fully generic), with its fixture test.
- **`node`** — the existing "`node --test` skips dot-directories" prose rule now has a check, `node/node-test-discovery`: an invocation whose arguments resolve to no path in the tree, in `package.json` scripts or a workflow step. Genuinely additive, so it ships with a new rehearsal fixture (`node-consumer`) rather than a migration record.
- **`claudinite-lifecycle`** — two prose rules on the canon access boundary: a file a canon module references but absent from the vendored mount is vendor-set evidence, not proof the canon lacks it; and a canon-level fix found from a session scoped to one repo goes on as a patch-block issue in that repo rather than a routed-around push.
- **`git-github` (git-github-advanced skill)** — `issue_write`'s `labels` field also full-overwrites, not just the body.
- **`claudinite-growth` (unattended-agents skill)** — two dispatched-subagent lessons: don't shadow a subagent's own read of a file it's analyzing while it's running, and search issues (not just git/PR state) before asserting no progress survived a lost subagent.

Each pack's `version` is bumped with a `VERSIONS.md` row in the same commit.

## Rejected (logged on the tracker)

- "The site describes itself in prose beyond its privacy claims — correct every self-description a behaviour change falsifies, in the same commit." Too close to the existing `basics` rule on changing what software does with a user's data (grep the surface for a claim the change makes false, reconcile every hit) — a narrowing to privacy vs. a widening to any self-description, not a distinct insight.
- "A `converge-item.mjs` failure from a session is a known gap; never hand-replicate it via `issue_write`'s full-overwrite `labels` field." The gap itself and its correct handling are already the queue's own `instructions.md` (step 6) and `converge-item.mjs`'s design; this restates known behaviour with new incident evidence rather than adding new guidance. (The general `issue_write` labels gotcha it surfaces *is* new and is promoted separately, above.)
- "A file missing from the mount is evidence about the vendor set... (2026-08-16/17 canon-not-shipped-it filings)" — same insight as the promoted claudinite-lifecycle rule; not a second item.

Verified: full suite green (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`) except the one pre-existing shallow-clone-limited test (`engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs`, fails identically on unmodified `main`); `check_the_world.mjs` and `check_the_work.mjs` both clean (0 blocking); rehearsal suite green including the new `node-consumer` shape.

{"number":1451,"title":"Promote lessons from ClaudiniteWebsite and Shepherd's local packs","body":"Growth-promote run over the two target members named in #1435's Context: **ClaudiniteWebsite** and **Shepherd**.

### Promoted (10)

| Origin | Rung | Landed | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| ClaudiniteWebsite | prose | `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md` | Finding a fix that belongs in the canon while working in a member repo: the scratch clone is read-only in practice (fetch works, push 403s) — that's org egress policy, not a bug to route around. Patch it as a diff on an issue in the member repo, never push, and never edit the vendored mount in place. |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | prose | `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md` | A file a vendored module references but that's absent from `.claudinite/shared/` is evidence about the vendor *set*, not the canon — check the canon itself before filing an issue claiming it was never shipped. |
| Shepherd | prose | `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/RULES.md` | Before pushing a change that touches workflows, `.claudinite-checks.json`, or pack config, run `check_the_world.mjs` locally — it's the same script CI's conformance job runs. |
| Shepherd | prose | `packs/basics/RULES.md` (Harness-tool contracts) | Check whether `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided before reaching for it, and batch every open decision into one call rather than asking serially. |
| Shepherd | prose | `packs/basics/RULES.md` (Harness-tool contracts) | Waiting on a subagent/task with nothing left to do — say so in plain text with no tool call; a manufactured no-op can come back with no visible text and force an interrupt. |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | prose (sharpen) | `unattended-agents` skill | Sharpens the shared-checkout rule: never amend a subagent's already-pushed commit or relay a fix instruction built from a misread of its in-flight state; if the checkout-back or the fix is itself refused by the permission classifier, that refusal is the tell a live subagent is using the checkout — don't force it. |
| ClaudiniteWebsite + Shepherd (independently) | prose | `unattended-agents` skill | Once a source is delegated to a background subagent, reading/re-analyzing it yourself while it runs is wasted work, not a safety net — wait on the dispatch or spend the interim elsewhere. |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | prose | `unattended-agents` skill | Before declaring a lost background subagent "made no progress" after a worker restart, check every channel it could have written to (issues, PRs, comments), not only git state and the dispatch thread's own comments. |
| Shepherd | prose | `unattended-agents` skill | Catching a flawed prompt right after dispatching a background subagent — resume it with a follow-up message, never a fresh redispatch over the identical source. |
| Shepherd | prose | `git-github-advanced` skill (sharpen + 2 new) | Sharpens the repo-allowlist rule with the scoped-vs-scopeless asymmetry (a repo-argument tool is denied outright when out of scope; a scopeless one like `search_code`/`search_issues` isn't and can still leak). Adds: `search_code`'s index can lag and undercount for an exhaustive enumeration; a multi-target sweep should `subscribe_pr_activity` on every PR it leaves open, not a sample. |

**Prose for all ten** — every one is in-flight judgment (which tool to reach for, whether to shadow a subagent, how to read a denial) or a tool/platform behavioral caveat with no repo-state signature a check could carry. No conformance-backlog issues opened.

### Notable rejections — already covered (dedup)

- ClaudiniteWebsite's "site describes itself in prose beyond its privacy claims" — already the general shape of `basics/RULES.md`'s "grep the whole surface for the standing absolutes it touches" (Changing what you do with user data).

Each item below is generalized from its origin repo's local pack, deduped against the whole corpus, and routed to the pack whose territory it falls in.

**web-speech** (from CrosswordChat/`browser-speech`)
- OS-rendered TTS (`chrome.tts`) bypasses the browser's own echo cancellation entirely, since AEC only attenuates audio the browser itself rendered — needs an application-level echo guard.

**basics** (from LaughCounter/`laughcounter`, Shepherd/`shepherd`, WIP/`wip`)
- Surface a shipped build's exact version+build identity from real build metadata, not a hand-maintained constant.
- Before dropping a carried-over aggregate `GENERATED` file on "the next run recomputes it", check the recompute's own inputs cover the same historical span.
- Edit a hand-maintained JSON config as anchored text, never a parse/re-serialize round-trip.
- A command block handed to the owner to paste into an interactive terminal carries no trailing `#` comment.

**node** (from GoogleCalendarEventCreator/`gcec`, hitbut, WIP)
- A throwaway script needing a real project dependency can't live in an external scratchpad.
- `btoa`/`atob` operate on Latin1 code units and throw or corrupt non-Latin1 text.
- Check what Node version CI actually pins before relying on a version-gated runtime feature.

**flutter** (from WIP/`wip`)
- Real file or image I/O inside `testWidgets` needs `tester.runAsync`, or the test hangs in the fake-async zone rather than failing.

**git-github** (from EdFringeNow, Shepherd, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, TLDR)
- `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation` widens from `schedule:` alone to also catch `workflow_run:`/`repository_dispatch:` triggers.
- `list_pull_requests`'s `merged` field is unreliable for landed-ness; `search_code` can undercount for exhaustive enumeration; subscribe every PR a sweep leaves open, not a sample; amend rather than rewrite history for a missing issue reference; stop re-probing for a confirmed-absent PR template.
- `actions_list`'s `list_workflow_runs` can ignore `per_page` entirely — don't retry it smaller (confirmed independently on two repos).
- `issue_read`'s `get_*` methods reject a PR number outright — use `pull_request_read`.

**claudinite-growth** (`unattended-agents` skill, from EdFringeNow, Shepherd, WIP)
- A dispatched subagent's "completed" notification can carry a placeholder final message rather than its real result.
- Check whether `AskUserQuestion`'s answer is already decided before firing it.
- A bare `wait` in its own Bash call waits on nothing — each invocation is a fresh shell.
- An until-loop satisfiable on its first check is a blind sleep in disguise.
- Resolving one wait through two mechanisms at once (a background timer plus direct polling) leaves the timer's own completion as a stray notification.

Every pack touched has its `version` bumped, a `VERSIONS.md` row, and (where its RULES.md changed) an updated README rule index. `node --test` on the full suite (2936 tests) and `check_the_world.mjs` both pass clean (0 blocking).

**Deferred to a sibling PR, not this one**: CrosswordChat's `host-page-adaptation` pack is a large, cohesive, genuinely uncovered practice ("driving a host page you don't own") that doesn't fit any existing pack's territory — already split into its own PR, #1525, per the promote task's own convention.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

    claudinite-dashboard: move the Pages deploy into a publish-pages task, leaving a four-step workflow (#1664)
    
    * claudinite-dashboard: move the Pages deploy into a publish-pages task
    
    The seeded workflow decided for itself when to republish (path-filtered
    push, a workflow_run catch-up, a cache key over the sources), built the
    site and carried the build's inputs — all frozen at adoption in every
    member. The publish-pages task owns that now: daily after the lifecycle
    update, gated on the mount or the declaration moving, it builds the
    site, force-pushes the tree as one root commit to gh-pages, dispatches
    the workflow and follows its run, parking as needs-human-action when
    the deploy fails with Pages not enabled.
    
    The stub keeps only what needs a workflow job — a deploy with source
    "GitHub Actions" needs an Actions artifact and a per-job OIDC token,
    neither of which a run: step's subprocess has — so it is
    workflow_dispatch and the four Pages actions, with no run: step, no
    Node and no variables. build-site keeps tasks/ out of the published
    tree. Version 60902.15.

1	# Working discipline
2	
3	- **Starting any requested change** — begin from the *problem*, not the solution, in any
4	  repository and not just this one. Reach an explicit shared understanding with the owner of the
5	  problem the change is meant to solve **and** agreement that the requested change is the best way
6	  to solve it; a different fix, or none, may serve better.
7	
8	- **Replying to an owner comment** — open with an explicit classification line,
9	  `Comment class: correction | feature | process-change | other`, where `other` covers questions,
10	  approvals and command phrases and a mixed comment names each part. An automation dispatch prompt
11	  is a comment too: class `other`, in your *first* substantive reply rather than at the end of the
12	  run. Put the class **alone on the line** and any explanation on the next one: the line is scanned
13	  for *every* class token on it, so restating the menu declares all of them. A class cannot be taken
14	  back, and a clean re-declaration further down does not override the first.
15	
16	- **Acting on a correction** — you misunderstood something. Repair the shared understanding, then
17	  rework what the misread already touched; the artifact changes as much as the correction demands,
18	  but a correction never adds a new requirement or rule.
19	
20	- **Acting on a feature** — agree on the requirement, record it in the project's requirements
21	  document (its executable spec, where it keeps one), write the test that proves it and watch it
22	  fail, then implement until it passes.
23	
24	- **Acting on a process change** — the owner is changing *how* work is done. Land it as durable
25	  rules in the project's local scope, its own local packs (in Claudinite itself, its packs), routed
26	  through the mechanism promotion ladder (platform setting → hook → check → skill → prose).
27	  Promoting a rule into the shared canon is the growth lifecycle's separate call, not the
28	  interactive session's.
29	
30	- **Choosing what goes on that ladder** — only a rule that constrains *how work is done* and
31	  outlives any one feature; a checkable signature doesn't earn a rule its place. Reject two shapes
32	  outright: a check that asserts particular code exists or still reads a particular way (it pins a
33	  point in time), and a rule derivable from the product's requirements (that is a requirement —
34	  take it to the feature path, the requirements document and the test that proves it).
35	
36	- **Landing a rule anywhere on the ladder** — author the assurance first, the check the future
37	  world must satisfy, execute it and watch it fail, and only then make the fixes that turn it green.
38	  At the prose rung, where no check can carry an in-flight judgment rule, the equivalent step is
39	  showing the corpus doesn't already cover the rule before writing it.
